memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Give the Levites to Aaron and his sons; they are the Israelites who are to be given wholly to him. Appoint Aaron and his sons to serve as priests; anyone else who approaches the sanctuary is to be put to death. - Num 3:9-10 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The Levites were to be given "wholly" to the service of God's house. There was no half-hearted involvement, no partial commitment. They belonged entirely to this holy work.

The word "wholly" is worth pausing on. God does not ask for a portion of our lives, a slice of our time, a corner of our hearts. He asks for all of us. The Levites picture what wholehearted devotion looks like — a life given completely to God's purposes.

The verse also carries a solemn warning: anyone unauthorised who approached the sanctuary would die. Again we meet the seriousness of God's holiness. Access to God was not casual; it was carefully guarded. This was not cruelty but protection, teaching Israel that a holy God cannot be approached however we please.

We should feel the weight of that before we rush past it. And yet, what stands closed here is thrown open in Christ. Through Jesus, our great High Priest, the way to God is now open to all who come through Him. The barrier that once meant death has been removed by His death (Eph 2:18).

So give yourself wholly to God, not out of fear, but out of love for the One who gave Himself wholly for you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Have you given yourself "wholly" to God, or only in part?
- What area of your life are you still holding back?
- How does Christ's full sacrifice inspire your full devotion?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, I want to belong to You wholly, not partly. Take every part of my life, and help me to hold nothing back from You. Amen.
